stories.title: A Utah nonprofit bought the Tillamook Air Museum's WWII blimp hangar for $1 — and saved it
stories.summary: Ten months after a December 2025 windstorm tore a roughly 200-by-30-foot hole in the roof of the historic WWII blimp hangar, the Vintage Aviation Museum of Spanish Fork, Utah, bought Hangar B — plus the Port of Tillamook Bay's aircraft, artifacts and equipment — for $1, and the museum reopened Oct 29. The Port kept the land on a long-term lease, FEMA covered 75% of the $542,000 debris cleanup, and a full reroof is still to come.
stories.img_credit: Photo of the museum's Mini Guppy in front of Hangar B by 7bd1118425 via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (licensed photo, News Scout batch 1, 2026-11-21).

stories.title: The Big Tree of Rockaway Beach: a 1,000-year-old cedar that survived the 1700 Cascadia quake and tsunami, hiding in plain sight
stories.summary: At the end of a one-mile ADA-accessible boardwalk through the Cedar Wetlands Nature Preserve in Rockaway Beach stands one of the largest Western Red Cedars in North America — an estimated 800 to 1,200 years old, 154 feet tall, with a 49-foot trunk circumference. The tree survived coastal storms, fires, earthquakes and the 1700 Cascadia tsunami, in a nearly 50-acre old-growth cedar wetland tucked inside a residential neighborhood.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Jordan Wolfe / Oregon Coast TODAY (the story's own photo).

stories.title: Tillamook grad wins a national FFA title with a flower business she started in high school
stories.summary: Tillamook High School graduate Tatum Lancaster was named the 2026 National FFA Agricultural Sales–Entrepreneurship Proficiency Award winner before 40,000 people at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis — Oregon's only first-place finish at the national convention. Her winning project, Western Grace Floral Co., is the floral design business she started as a junior in a floriculture class and still runs while attending Oregon State University.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Tillamook Headlight Herald (the story's own photo).

stories.title: Mother-daughter duo help fill tables and feed Tillamook County at Thanksgiving
stories.summary: A mother and daughter are behind a Thanksgiving effort that puts hundreds of dinners on tables across Tillamook County. Two generations are cooking for neighbors who might otherwise go without on the holiday.
stories.img_credit: Image: Tillamook County Pioneer (the story's own art — the Nehalem Bay Methodist Church community dinner flyer).

stories.title: The Lasagnathon: all-you-can-eat lasagna, four kinds, live music, at the Bay City Arts Center
stories.summary: Bay City Arts Center's annual Lasagnathon fundraiser returns Saturday, Dec 5: one $40 ticket buys unlimited helpings of four kinds of lasagna — meat, veggie, gluten-free and vegan. The evening includes live music from Matt Didlake and a silent auction of local art.
stories.img_credit: Artwork: Bay City Arts Center event poster, via Tillamook County Pioneer.

stories.title: Neah-Kah-Nie students named their robotics team ‘Tsunami Zone’ — and competed at Hillsboro
stories.summary: The Neah-Kah-Nie middle school and high school robotics team — competing under the name ‘Tsunami Zone’ — took part in Meet 1 at Hillsboro on Nov 14. The students wrote up the competition themselves for the Pioneer, photos and all.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Arabella C. and Addison C. / Tillamook County Pioneer (student photos from the story).

stories.title: Consejo Hispano's Magia Navideña: holiday gifts for local families, from local givers
stories.summary: Consejo Hispano's annual Holiday Gift Giving Program, Magia Navideña, is underway: community members sponsor a local child and shop for their holiday wishes, bringing a little extra alegría and warmth to families across Tillamook County. Givers are thanked with a Cerveza y Chocolate donor celebration.
